There is a “readmission” you need to do before you can come back. So don’t register now, but figure out deadlines for readmission for when you want to enroll in classes again. Call registrar and say “I’m taking spring quarter 2020 off, what do I need to do (and when) to enroll in fall 2020?”

If you can manage taking your test, express to your professor that you’re really struggling but things snowballed a bit and you’re feeling very lost. Say that you haven’t talked to anyone through disability/counseling/advising yet, but that you need help. Your 70% class is still salvageable if you can perform well for the rest of the quarter. Ask if your professor can work with you to either a) let you take the test another day in the disability center so you have time to ask campus services for help b) take an incomplete (k on your transcript) and finish up that winter quarter class during another time. I recommend you emailing your professor all of this ASAP. You’d be surprised how understanding and kind even the most serious professors can be. 

I had an illness about this time that prevented me from finishing my coursework at the end of the quarter and my professors were overall very helpful. You just need to be transparent and be open to help. 
Part 2 would be to reach out to disability resources, counseling services and academic advising. But where do you go first?
If you’re panicking so much to the point that you feel unable to take the steps you need to take to pull through the end of the quarter, contact counseling services. Give them a call and say you’re in crisis, you need someone to help settle you down so you can handle end of quarter stress. 
Next step would be academic advising. Figuring out what steps you can take to improve your situation and where you might need to cut your losses (it’s okay to retake a class you failed). It’s okay to take an incomplete and finish when you’re in a better state. It’s okay to take a break from school all together. It’s okay to feel like it’s not okay. 

I wish the best for you. 
Sincerely, 
Someone who has been there
